messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate + 429s observed for org=aurora-203. Spike started ~16:18 UTC. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/aurora-203/spike — paging SRE oncall

sre-jordan: ack — I'll take this, looking at logs now

support-amy: customer-reported: >90% of requests getting 429s in last 5m, ticket #12345, they say real-time features are impacted

eng-runtime: seeing lots of concurrent long-generation requests from aurora-203 hitting the hosted pool; tail shows KV cache misses + model fallback thrash

sre-lee: quick triage: org qps jumped from ~3.2k to ~24k. Cluster-level throttles started to cascade. Recommend temporary org-level RL bump + traffic shaping to protect control plane

sre-jordan: agree. I'll apply emergency bump and add a short traffic-shape rule to deprioritize >1k token responses. Executing now.

sre-jordan: ```/orgs/aurora-203/rate_limit set --qps=6000 --burst=12000 --reason "emergency spike 2026-03-17 16:18 UTC"```

incident-bot: change accepted — request queued by ops-runner (id: ops-8492)

sre-jordan: ops-runner: applied change — status: OK, applied at 16:19:11 UTC

support-amy: pinged customer: asked them to pause non-critical batch jobs and throttle back clients where possible :pray:

eng-runtime: enabling short-priority rule via routing config. Snippet:```route: aurora-203 priority: high if tokens<=1024 else low; cache-prefix: enabled``` applying now

sre-lee: monitoring metrics — 5xxs and 429s dropping. If stable, keep bump for a short window then step down gradually. Also raising alert to product for quota escalation request

sre-jordan: current numbers: errors down from 85% -> 3% within ~60s. Latency normalized. :thumbsup:

support-amy: customer confirms decreased errors and that critical features are back online. They're worried about recurring spikes and asked about a permanent quota change

sre-lee: Plan: 1) maintain temporary bump for 15m 2) run targeted sampling to find heavy callers in org 3) coordinate with product for formal quota request + safety guardrails 4) schedule postmortem

sre-jordan: documenting change and rationale in ops-runner entry. Will handoff monitoring to next oncall @sre-maya at 16:40 UTC

incident-bot: Handoff: oncall -> sre-maya recorded at 16:32:00 UTC by sre-jordan

sre-maya: ack — I'll take it from here, watching traffic and the ops-runner logs. If errors trend back up, I'll escalate to runtime eng for a targeted throttling rule per-client

eng-runtime: follow-up: we saw a small subset of clients doing aggressive retry loops after 429s. We'll propose adding jitter + backoff guidance to the SDK and a server-side short-circuit for heavy clients

support-amy: created customer follow-up ticket and linked to this thread. Customer asked for timeline on quota review, flagged as P2

sre-jordan: leaving a note: revert plan -> after 15m stable, step down to 4k QPS for 10m, then back to baseline (3k) and open ticket for sustained quota increase if warranted

sre-maya: monitored 15m window, spike subsided. Proceeding with staged rollback now.```/orgs/aurora-203/rate_limit set --qps=4000 --burst=8000 --reason "stepdown after stabilization"``` applied at 16:51:00 UTC

sre-maya: final step to baseline in 10m if metrics remain healthy. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with product/support for quota request

incident-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated). Summary: emergency org RL bump + traffic shaping prevented broader cluster impact. Follow-ups: postmortem, SDK retry guidance, quota review (ticket #PM-567)

support-amy: customer updated and thanked the team. Closing customer-facing incident update

sre-maya: closing internal thread — will post postmortem link when ready
